sentences.text: This is first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of regular bail in connection with crime No.303/2024 dated : not mentioned, registered at P.S. - Industrial Area District - Dewas for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 376(3), 376(2)(N), 450, 323, 506(II) of IPC and Section 5L/6, 3/4(2) of POCSO Act.
2. As per prosecution case, it is alleged that the applicant had abducted a minor girl and committed rape with her.

sentences.text: 3. Counsel for the applicant submits that as per the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, the prosecutrix was a consenting party and thereafter the applicant and the complainant/respondent no.2 have got married.
In this regard a certificate of Arya Samaj has been filed.
It is also stated that the prosecutrix has become major.
4. Counsel for the respondent No.2/prosecutrix submits the prosecutrix has no objection to the prayer for grant of bail.

5. Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail and submits that in the statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C the prosecutrix has made specific allegation against the applicant and stated that a video was prepared and she was threatened that the said video will be made viral.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix was minor on the date of incident.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and considering the no objection by the counsel for the prosecutrix in which it is stated that the prosecutrix has become major and the applicant and the prosecutrix have got married.
There is no seizure of any video as alleged by the prosecution.
In view of the aforesaid, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled for grant of bail.

7. It is directed that applicant Yash shall be released from custody upon furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Ld. Court below.
8. A typed copy of this order is being forwarded to the Office of the Advocate General, on their email address, for intimation to the Police Station concerned.
The office is requested to forward a copy of this order to the Ld. Court below.
9. With the aforesaid, the application is allowed and disposed off.
Cc as per rules.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE PK Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87517531/
